function: Learns 3D positions and excitation current weights of UAVs in a virtual antenna array for collaborative beamforming to a remote base station, trading rate against energy (p. 7).
system: 16 single-antenna rotary-wing UAVs forming a virtual array in a 100x100 m area at 100-120 m altitude, air-to-ground link to far-field BS, 2.4 GHz, no RIS (pp. 3, 11).
method: HATRPO-UCB, multi-agent deep reinforcement learning: one actor-critic per UAV, Beta-distribution policy, observation enhancement; trained offline on a central server, executed online (pp. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator, no dataset: probabilistic LoS/NLoS air-to-ground model (C=10, D=0.6), path-loss exponent 2, attenuation 3 and 23 dB; no 3GPP model or measurements (pp. 4, 7, 11).
test_conditions: Trained 4x10^5 single-slot episodes, served BS may change per episode (p. 9); evaluated on two BSs, 16 UAVs, one 100x100 m area; no other scenarios (pp. 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: LAA and RAA (symmetric linear and rectangular arrays); learned: MADDPG, IPPO, MAPPO, conventional HATRPO (p. 12).
metrics: Average episode reward and energy during training, transmission rate (bps) and propulsion energy (J) for two BSs, critic loss, rate under phase errors (pp. 12-15).
complexity: Analytic orders for training (terms in lt, lbt, nepi, lconj) and for inference, O(n_uav * sum z_{i-1} z_i), stated; no measured runtime or FLOPs (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "the LoS probability can be modeled as [32]" is a probabilistic air-to-ground model with C=10, D=0.6 (p. 7) and path-loss exponent 2 (p. 11); a custom simulator, with no 3GPP model and no measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "the UVAA may communicate with different remote BSs at various episodes" describes training; p. 13: "communicating continuously with two BSs" is the only test, and the paper never says these BSs, the 16 UAVs, or the area differ from training.
q3_support: p. 12: "LAA: All UAVs form a linear antenna array (LAA)" is the non-learned baseline and p. 12: "MADDPG: Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG)" a standard learned one; p. 13: "Table 3 shows the numerical optimization results of various methods" reports rate and energy for all.
q4_support: p. 11: "Complexity of training. For nuav agents" and p. 11: "Complexity of inference. In the implementation phase" give analytic orders of complexity of the proposed method for training and for inference.
q5_support: p. 11: "We implement simulations in an environment with Python 3.8 and Pytorch 1.10" describes a custom simulator; no code or data link appears in the 18 pages, and the appendices sit in a supplemental file that is not linked.
notes: arXiv v1 preprint. The text extractor scrambles pages 16-18 (the real page 16 is split across them, real pages 17-18 are missing), so those pages were read as images: end of Section 6.2, Fig. 11, Conclusion, references, biographies, with no code or data statement. Area 6: the actions set UAV positions (above the physical layer) and excitation current weights (beam control of an aerial link), so the work passes the above_phy check, and area 6 wins over area 3 by the specificity order. q2 is borderline: p. 13 says the trained networks serve the second BS directly, but the paper never says that BS lies outside the training range. q3 counts MADDPG, IPPO and MAPPO; conventional HATRPO is a variant of the proposed method and does not count.
